title: KV economy: MLA, windows, sinks, and eviction
brief: Count MLA's latent bytes, show the absorbed form matches the naive one, hold a rolling window with sinks against masked attention, and evict with H2O against an oracle.
hints: MLA caches the latent (d_c) and one shared RoPE key (d_rope) per layer per token. Forgetting the RoPE key gives 61,440 bytes for DeepSeek-V2, not 69,120.
The absorbed form reads the cache directly. Multiply the query by W_UK first, so scores are q_lat dot c_kv. Apply W_UV after the weighted sum of the latents. The scale stays 1/sqrt(d_h + d_r).
Token p >= sinks goes to slot sinks + (p - sinks) % window. The first `sinks` slots are never overwritten. The window counts the current token.
H2O softmaxes each query over the cached keys only, adds those probabilities to every cached key's score, and evicts the lowest score outside the newest `recent` tokens.
